newsitem.title: USA: Air Force suspends training off east coast.
newsitem.headline: Air Force suspends training off east coast.

text.p: The Air Force on Friday suspended flight operations in designated training areas off the East Coast after two incidents this week involving close brushes between civilian planes and F-16 fighter jets.

The order was made by Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ronald Fogelman, who said the operations would be suspended in "designated warning areas" normally set aside for training flights until all units had reviewed procedures with the Federal Aviation Administration and other agencies.
The brief announcement said that the stand-down of operations included active duty, reserve and national guard aircraft.

Earlier on Friday, an American Eagle pilot reported that four District of Columbia Air National Guard F-16 jets flew "too close" to his passenger plane off Maryland in the second such incident involving civilian and military planes this week.

In an incident on Wednesday off New Jersey, the operator of a Boeing 727 charter jet with about 80 passengers said it had a near collision with two F-16s. It maneuvered violently in response to electronic cockpit warnings when it was approached by one of the fighter jets.
